about.title: Healdsburg Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Healdsburg is a small town, and a sudden death here is felt far beyond one household. Roughly 11,700 people live within city limits, so the person you lost was likely known on Healdsburg Avenue, along Dry Creek Road, or by the neighbors who share your street. Public records show that in 2025 the city logged 18 injury collisions and 21 people hurt, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. Yet wrongful death cases in Sonoma County arise from more than local roads: a crash on US-101, a fall at a worksite, a medication error, or neglect in a care setting can all lead to a civil claim. Under California law, a spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring that claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The filing deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a government agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Healdsburg families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can focus on grieving while someone else focuses on the paperwork.

items.question: Healdsburg recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim covers any death caused by negligence, not only local road crashes. Healdsburg residents commute along US-101, work in vineyards and construction, receive medical care across Sonoma County, and may have relatives in care facilities. Any of those settings can give rise to a claim, regardless of where the death physically occurred.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil action that is entirely separate from any criminal prosecution. The two can move forward at the same time, and a criminal outcome does not decide the civil claim. An attorney can explain how evidence from one may be relevant to the other.

items.question: What losses can a family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's situation is different, so no one can predict a specific figure. An attorney will look at your household's circumstances before discussing what may be pursued.
